children: According to Sina Finance, Jefferies said three risks threaten the AI investment boom driving emerging-market stock gains in 2026: higher financing costs, weakening momentum in earnings estimate upgrades, and slower data-center capital spending. It expects emerging-market stocks to perform poorly in early 2027 and recommends investors adjust their asset allocations.

Emerging-market stocks have gained about 8% this year, while South Korean stocks have risen nearly 40%, largely on earnings growth at AI-related companies. Those companies now account for about 46% of the MSCI Emerging Markets Index, while their advantage in earnings estimate upgrades over other sectors is narrowing.

Jefferies said large technology companies’ heavy capital spending has raised questions about investment returns. Higher financing costs and challenges to data-center profitability could prompt them to cut spending, hurting upstream semiconductor and hardware suppliers. The firm downgraded South Korean equities to underweight and raised Indian equities to overweight.

Jefferies forecasts earnings per share for emerging-market listed companies to grow 25.9% in 2027, below the 27.7% market consensus, with growth slowing to 12% in 2028. It said tighter financial conditions and weaker momentum in earnings estimate upgrades could weigh on stocks in early 2027, despite more attractive valuations after a recent market correction. It sees about 25% upside over the medium to long term as financial conditions improve and valuations recover.

Jefferies retains some AI-related stocks, including Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, but plans to focus more on sustainable earnings growth, capital-spending discipline, and returns on invested capital. Its strategy is shifting from pursuing AI infrastructure spending to favoring quality companies, beneficiaries of AI adoption, and firms with sustainable dividend capacity.

title: Jefferies Warns AI Investment Slowdown Could Hurt Emerging Markets, Downgrades South Korea to Underweight
